subject: Request: per-tenant soft-delete window & physical-region pinning for PharmaX
messages:
From: Anna Laurent <anna.laurent@pharmax.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: security@pharmax.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Initial questions on geo-locking and soft-delete windows for PHX-ENT-01

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and privacy folks had a few follow-ups while we scope the procurement for PHX-ENT-01. Two core asks:

1) Can Redwood support per-tenant configurable soft-delete (e.g., 30/90/365 days) where data is retained in a recoverable state before final purge? We need to map this to our SOPs for e-discovery.
2) Critical: we require physical-region pinning (US-only) for all persisted artifacts related to model input/outputs for the tenant. That includes any cached prefixes, KV entries, and object-store archives.

Attached is our condensed data handling requirements and a small field mapping CSV showing which data classes are in-scope. Can you confirm feasibility and any implementation timeline?

Best,
Anna
Anna Laurent
Head of Security Programs
PharmaX Therapeutics

Attachments: PharmaX-Data-Handling-Requirements.pdf, requested-field-mapping.csv

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Anna Laurent <anna.laurent@pharmax.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions on geo-locking and soft-delete windows for PHX-ENT-01

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Quick answers up front:

- Per-tenant soft-delete windows: yes, we can expose a configurable retention window (soft-delete) at the tenant level with options like 30/90/365 days. That will surface in the Admin API and Console as a retention flag that governs purge scheduling; meanwhile data remains recoverable during the soft-delete window.

- Physical-region pinning (US-only): architecturally possible, but there are a few nuance items we need to align on:
  * Which artifacts must be geo-locked: ephemeral KV cache, persisted prefix cache, object-store archives, logs, and backups?
  * Are legal-hold/e-discovery holds expected to override purge windows?
  * Do you require cryptographic key material to be restricted to a US KMS/HSM?

I'm looping in Irene (security/product) and Dylan (infra/serving) to provide feasibility notes and a rough timeline. I'll follow up with a short mutual action plan.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on geo-locking and soft-delete windows for PHX-ENT-01

Thanks for the tag, Rachel. High-level product/security notes:

- Soft-delete: We already support tenant-scoped retention policies for ephemeral artifacts in our roadmap, but current implementation purges at the object-store level and doesn't present a self-serve soft-delete restore in the Console. We can add an intermediate "recoverable" state API for 30/90/365 windows; this requires changes in the lifecycle controller and the retention metadata index. Estimated: 6-8 weeks for an opt-in beta if prioritized.

- Geo-locking: Two layers: control-plane annotation and data-plane enforcement. Control-plane tagging we can do quickly (metadata flags); enforcement requires ensuring storage and cache slices are pinned to US-only AZs, and that cross-region replication is disabled for the tenant. Also need to guarantee backups and snapshots honor the setting. Estimated: 8-12 weeks to provide a hardened US-only path with audit logs, shorter if we can accept manual process controls in the interim.

- Legal hold/e-discovery: We should support legal-hold markers that supersede retention-based purge. That implies a second metadata flag and retention workflow changes. Add 1-2 sprints to the timeline above.

I've added a preliminary list of actionable items below for engineering. Dylan — can you confirm feasibility of pinning KV and prefix caches to a region and whether current autoscaling policies would interfere?

Irene
Irene Choi
Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Laurent <anna.laurent@pharmax.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on geo-locking and soft-delete windows for PHX-ENT-01

Short technical reply from infra/runtime:

- KV/prefix cache: We can introduce tenant affinity so cache shards are allocated on US-only pools. That requires adding tenant placement keys to the autoscaler and ensuring shard migration respects geo-lock flags. Implementation effort: ~3 weeks engineering + 1 week QA.

- Object storage: We will provide a tenant-storage-policy that pins to a US-only storage class and disables cross-region replication. Work: ~2-3 weeks to surface policy in Console and enforce in provisioning.

- Backups/snapshots: Need immediate change to backup job to check tenant policy and skip cross-region copies; small change but needs careful testing. ~1 week.

- Auditability: We'll emit audit events when retention or geo-lock flags are changed and when purge jobs run; add a retention-run audit entry for legal hold overrides. ~2 weeks.

Edge cases: if the tenant later requests region migration (e.g., EU), we'll need a controlled export+import path; that's out-of-scope for the initial go-live.

Plan proposal: Beta (opt-in) for US-only geo-lock + configurable soft-delete (no self-serve restore) in 6 weeks; full self-serve restore + legal-hold override in 10-12 weeks.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Anna Laurent <anna.laurent@pharmax.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on geo-locking and soft-delete windows for PHX-ENT-01

Thanks all — that roadmap and timeline look reasonable. A few follow-ups before we mark this as an accept: 

1) Can you include KMS/HSM residency constraints in the US-only deliverable? We need assurances that tenant keys (for encryption-at-rest) do not leave the US boundary.
2) For the beta release, we are comfortable with an opt-in setup and a support-assisted restore flow, provided SLAs for restore and a documented playbook.
3) Please share a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones, owners, and acceptance criteria so our procurement and legal teams can proceed.

If you can get the MAP and the KMS note by EOD Monday, we can move to the commercial redline stage next week.

Best,
Anna
PharmaX Security
